newTheorem.statement: For every m, base-7 integers using digits [0, 1, 2] form a pairwise-distinct [1,-3,2]-free set of size 3^m below 7^m; hence exponent log_7(3)=0.564575034054>1/2.
newTheorem.proof: The all-length digit/carry product has no accepting state. Word counting gives |D|^m and the magnitude bound B^m.

exactRejectionBoundary.scope: memoryless fixed-digit alphabets, bases 3..16, normalized to contain 0
exactRejectionBoundary.result: no exponent >1/2 found; base 9 size 3 attains exactly 1/2
exactRejectionBoundary.notClaimed: global impossibility for arbitrary finite-state languages

compressedExplanation: The compiler did beat 1/2—on a new compatible three-variable relation. On C3 itself it refused to manufacture a gain: the exact declared memoryless search class still tops out at the already banked square-root construction.
